svg.aria-label: The citric acid cycle as a wheel of structures. Step 1, citrate synthase: acetyl CoA (2 carbons) and water join oxaloacetate to make citrate, releasing CoA-SH. Step 2, aconitase: citrate is rearranged to isocitrate. Step 3, isocitrate dehydrogenase: NAD+ is reduced to NADH and CO2 leaves, giving alpha-ketoglutarate. Step 4, alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase: NAD+ is reduced to NADH and CO2 leaves, giving succinyl CoA. Step 5, succinyl CoA synthetase: GDP and phosphate make GTP, giving succinate. Step 6, succinate dehydrogenase: FAD is reduced to FADH2, giving fumarate. Step 7, fumarase: water adds, giving malate. Step 8, malate dehydrogenase: NAD+ is reduced to NADH, regenerating oxaloacetate. Per turn: 2 CO2, 3 NADH, 1 FADH2 and 1 GTP.

svg.text: The citric acid cycle (one turn, per acetyl CoA)
Each arrow is one step; the number matches the step close-ups in this section. Changed groups are highlighted there.
Per glucose the cycle turns twice (2 acetyl CoA), so double every number.
